results.content: Research Contents explore influence factors, theory-practice gap, cultural influences, interdisciplinary collaboration, and innovative art therapy systems, concluding with strategy research.](https://www.frontiersin.org/files/Articles/1617700/xml-images/fpsyg-16-1617700-g014.webp)[View in article](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1617700/full#fig14). The historical development of art therapy and its origins can be traced back to _Bildnerei der Geisteskranken_ by Hans Prinzhorn, a German art historian and psychiatric researcher ([Prinzhorn, 1923](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1617700/full#ref35)). With the maturity of the theory and changes in social needs, the application of art therapy has gradually extended from clinical psychology to a broader range of non-medical scenarios, such as education and community counseling, forming a diversified system of practice ([Naumburg, 1955](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1617700/full#ref32)). Among them, the American Art Therapy Association is significant in the history of art therapy, and the Wisconsin Art Therapy Association (WATA), led by Wayne Ramirez, has led to an inclusive definition that guarantees the equal development of the fields of psychiatry, education, and community practice ([Potash, 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1617700/full#ref34)). Together, these practices paint a rich picture of the development of art therapy worldwide, as detailed in [Table 1](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1617700/full#tab1).

results.title: Global Trends in Social Inclusion and Social Inclusion Policy
results.content: Regardless, while theorists such as Silver (Reference Silver1994, Reference Silver2015), Ruth Levitas (Reference Levitas2005) and Lyons and Huegler (Reference Lyons, Huegler, Healy and Link2012) have developed typologies of social inclusion by characterising national conceptualisations of the concept, there exists a gap in the literature on whether these conceptualisations have culminated in regimes that have operationalised the concepts through social inclusion policy, how different approaches to social inclusion policy relate to social exclusion, and global trends in the development of social inclusion policy. Following the Prepared Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis guidelines (Moher *et al*., Reference Moher, Liberati, Tetzlaff and Altman2009), we employed a systematic review to identify relevant studies in the databases Social Service Abstracts, ERIC, PsycINFO Academic Search Complete, EconLit, PAIS Index, Worldwide Political Science Abstracts, and Google Scholar using (‘social inclusion’ OR ‘social exclusion’) AND (‘international trends’ OR ‘global trends’) for our first research question and (‘social inclusion policy’) OR (‘social exclusion policy’) and (‘social inclusion policy’ OR ‘social exclusion policy’) AND (‘international trends’ OR ‘global trends’) for the second research question.
